title: Blackstone COO: AI boom is 'different' from previous investment cycles
excerpt: Erik McGregor/Getty Images Blackstone does not expect growing competition to drive down returns on its new investments in AI infrastructure, at least not any...
content_html:
Erik McGregor/Getty Images

Blackstone does not expect growing competition to drive down returns on its new investments in AI infrastructure, at least not anytime soon, said COO Jon Gray.

Speaking during the firm's Q2 earnings call, Gray said demand for data centers, chips and the power to supply them is so great that the risk of oversupply and a subsequent collapse in valuations is minimal.

"It's very hard to get the chips today, it's very hard to get the power, it's very hard to get the entitlements [to build data centers]," he added. "That means the supply is not matching [demand]."

Data centers are sufficiently large and complicated to build that you don't see what Gray described as a "Miami condo effect," where developers speculatively build capacity in the hope of finding a buyer.

Blackstone has the land, power and permissions to accommodate an estimated $200 billion in new data centers, Gray said.

"It's a very different dynamic than typical investment cycles ... where something generates very high returns and then you get an enormous supply shock coming back the other way, which drives down returns," he said.

Gray's comments come amid signs of cooling in the AI infrastructure boom.

The PHLX Semiconductor index, which tracks the aggregate share price of semiconductor manufacturers, is down by around 16% from its June 22 peak, after climbing nearly 99% in the six months leading up to that point.

Meta and SpaceX have both agreed to rent out their computing power capacity to other hyperscalers. While "a weak signal" in itself, such deals "signal overcapacity in the near term," Aswath Damodaran, professor of finance at New York University's Stern School of Business, told PitchBook earlier this month.

The exits of AI and energy assets drove a 27% increase in net realizations for Blackstone in Q2, compared with the same period last year, helping boost the firm's distributable earnings by 26% to $1.98 billion.

Blackstone realized $11 billion in investments in its corporate PE portfolio, including the sale of a control stake in Sabre Industries to the impact investing arm of TPG. Texas-based Sabre designs and manufactures electrical transmission and distribution infrastructure for the power utilities, data center and telecom sectors.

The firm's real estate portfolio produced $6.6 billion in realizations during the quarter—including the sale of three fully leased Northern Virginia data centers to Digital Realty Trust for $3.5 billion in cash and shares.

Gray said Blackstone is attracting strong interest from buyers for its AI and AI-related businesses, and fairly strong interest for AI-resistant businesses, in sectors such as fast food and medical supplies.

埃里克·麦格雷戈/盖蒂图片社

黑石集团首席运营官 Jon Gray 表示，预计日益激烈的竞争不会降低其人工智能基础设施新投资的回报，至少不会很快。

格雷在该公司第二季度财报电话会议上表示，对数据中心、芯片及其供电的需求如此之大，以至于供应过剩和随后估值暴跌的风险很小。

“如今获得芯片非常困难，获得电力非常困难，获得[建设数据中心]的权利也非常困难，”他补充道。 “这意味着供应与[需求]不匹配。”

数据中心规模足够大，建设起来也很复杂，你看不到格雷所说的“迈阿密公寓效应”，即开发商投机性地建设容量，希望找到买家。

Gray 表示，Blackstone 拥有土地、电力和许可，可以容纳价值约 2000 亿美元的新数据中心。

“这是一种与典型投资周期截然不同的动态...... 有些东西会产生非常高的回报，然后你会受到巨大的供应冲击，从而降低回报，”他说。

格雷发表上述言论之际，人工智能基础设施热潮有降温迹象。

跟踪半导体制造商总股价的 PHLX 半导体指数较 6 月 22 日的峰值下跌了约 16%，此前的六个月里上涨了近 99%。

Meta 和 SpaceX 均同意将其计算能力出租给其他超大规模企业。 纽约大学斯特恩商学院金融学教授阿斯瓦斯·达莫达兰(Aswath Damodaran)本月早些时候告诉PitchBook，虽然其本身是“一个微弱的信号”，但此类交易“表明了近期产能过剩”。

人工智能和能源资产的退出推动黑石第二季度净变现较去年同期增长 27%，帮助公司可分配收益增长 26% 至 19.8 亿美元。

Blackstone 在其企业私募股权投资组合中实现了 110 亿美元的投资，其中包括将 Sabre Industries 的控股权出售给 TPG 的影响力投资部门。 总部位于德克萨斯州的 Sabre 为电力公司、数据中心和电信行业设计和制造输电和配电基础设施。

该公司的房地产投资组合在本季度实现了 66 亿美元的变现，其中包括以 35 亿美元的现金和股票向 Digital Realty Trust 出售三个完全租赁的北弗吉尼亚数据中心。

格雷表示，黑石正在吸引买家对其人工智能和人工智能相关业务的浓厚兴趣，以及对快餐和医疗用品等行业的抗人工智能业务的浓厚兴趣。
